_comments: bc-aidp-next-golive#207, the tester's third comment: 'Deal Status Type' -> 'Status' and
'Forecast Category Type' -> 'Forecast Category'.
THE ROW THAT MATTERS IS THE VIRTUAL NAME FIELD, NOT THE FOREIGN KEY, and getting that wrong is
silent. mj-form-field resolves an FK's label through RelatedEntityNameFieldMap BEFORE the field's
own DisplayName (form-field.component.ts: it returns nameField.DisplayNameOrName and only falls
through to FieldInfo.DisplayNameOrName afterwards), and the baseline maps DealStatusTypeID ->
'DealStatusType' and ForecastCategoryTypeID -> 'ForecastCategoryType'. So relabelling the ...TypeID
rows applies cleanly, asserts successfully, and changes nothing anyone sees.
Measured against the database before writing this: DealStatusType reads 'Deal Status Type' and
DealStatusTypeID reads 'Deal Status Type ID'. The tester's 'Current label' column says 'Deal Status
Type' -- the virtual field -- which is the tell that these are the rows they meant.
AutoUpdateDisplayName goes to 0 so the label is a deliberate choice rather than something derived
from the column name if the column is ever renamed. CodeGen does not otherwise revert DisplayName:
spUpdateExistingEntityFieldsFromSchema never writes it (unlike Description), and
updateEntityFieldDisplayNameWhereNull is gated on the value being NULL.
bc-aidp-next-golive#259 item 7: 'Currency ID, Contract ID, Renews Contract ID, etc. won't have
"ID" in the label. There may be others too.' There are: measured against the database, every row
below reads with a trailing 'ID', and two acronyms read worse than that.
THESE ARE THE FK ROWS THEMSELVES, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE TWO ENTRIES ABOVE, and the
difference is not a style choice -- it is which row mj-form-field actually reads. It resolves an
FK's label through RelatedEntityNameFieldMap FIRST and only falls through to the field's own
DisplayName when there is no map. The two entries above relabel VIRTUAL NAME FIELDS because
DealStatusTypeID and ForecastCategoryTypeID both have one. Every field below has
RelatedEntityNameFieldMap = NULL, so its own DisplayName is what renders. Getting this backwards
asserts successfully and changes nothing anyone sees, in either direction.
WHY THE MAP IS NULL ON EACH, because the reasons differ and one of them may not hold forever:
- CurrencyID, ContractID, RenewsContractID are SOFT foreign keys. A soft FK gives the field a
related entity but no virtual name column in the base view, so no map is ever produced.
Verified on a database where the contract soft FK is already applied: still NULL.
- CampaignID has no related entity at all.
- PrimaryContactID and BillingContactID are HARD foreign keys with
IncludeRelatedEntityNameFieldInBaseView = 1 -- CodeGen wants a name column and cannot produce
one, because Sales Contacts' name field (DisplayNameAndEmail) is itself virtual, added by the
app-owned wrapper view that the generated Deal view does not join. If that ever changes, these
two labels go quiet and the virtual field becomes the row to set. Nothing warns; check the map
before assuming a relabel here still lands.
MRR and ARR are not FK fields and not about the 'ID' suffix at all. They are here because the same
audit found them: CodeGen's display-name derivation title-cases the column name, so the two figures
a rep reads most often render as 'Mrr' and 'Arr'.
AutoUpdateDisplayName goes to 0 on every row for the reason the first entry gives: the label becomes
a deliberate choice rather than something re-derived from the column name.
